paragraphs.text: March 11. The Life of Gregory, Pope of Rome. Blessed Gregory was appointed patriarch of God's holy Church in Rome. Before becoming patriarch, he was a monk in the monastery of the holy apostle Andrew, called Clivus Scauri, near the holy martyrs John and Paul. He was the abbot of that monastery. His mother, blessed Silvia, lived near the gate of the holy apostle Paul, at a place called Cella Nova. This blessed Gregory, while he was sitting in his cell and writing, was visited by a poor man, who begged him, saying, “Have mercy on me, servant of God Most High, for I was the captain of a ship,

and we were shipwrecked and lost much property, both our own and other people's.” The lover of the poor and true servant of Christ called his attendant and said to him, “Brother, go and give this man six gold coins.” The brother went and did as Gregory, the servant of God, had commanded him, and gave the poor man six gold coins, and he went away. Then, after waiting a little while, on that same day, the same poor man came to blessed Gregory, saying, “Have mercy on me, servant of God Most High, for I have lost much, but you have given me little.” The blessed man called his attendant and said to him, “Go, brother, give him another six gold coins.” The brother did so. The poor man took the twelve gold coins and went away. After waiting a little while again, he came to blessed Gregory for the third time that same day, saying, “Have mercy on me, servant of God Most High. Give me another blessing, for I have lost much.” The blessed man called his attendant and said to him, “Go and give him another six gold coins.” But he answered, saying, “Believe me, venerable father, there is not a single gold coin left in the treasury.” The blessed man said to him, “Do you not have some other vessel, or a garment, to give him?” He answered and said, “I have no other vessel, venerable father, except the silver dish which the noble lady sent with beans.”

Gregory, the servant of God, said to him, “Go, brother, give him that dish.” The brother did as the blessed man commanded him and gave it to the poor man. The poor man took the twelve gold coins and the silver dish and went away. When they appointed him patriarch of the holy Church in Rome, in accordance with patriarchal custom, he commanded his treasurer one day to bring twelve poor men together. to his table to dine with him. The treasurer did as the patriarch had commanded him. He invited twelve poor men. But when they sat down with the patriarch, there were found to be thirteen at the table. He summoned the treasurer and said to him, “Did I not tell you to invite twelve? How, then, have you invited thirteen without my command?” When the treasurer heard this, he was frightened and answered him, “Believe me, honored master, there are twelve of them.” No one could see the thirteenth except the patriarch alone. As they dined, the patriarch could see the thirteenth man sitting at the end of the table. And behold, his face changed its appearance: sometimes he looked like a gray-haired man, and sometimes like a youth. When they rose from the table, the blessed man dismissed all the others, but the thirteenth man, whose appearance was so wondrous, he took by the hand and brought into his own room, saying

to him, “I adjure you by the great power of God Almighty: tell me who you are and what your name is.” He said to him, “As for your asking my name, that too is a wonder. But I am the poor man who came to you when you were in the monastery of the holy apostle Andrew, called Clivus Scauri, when you were sitting in your cell writing, to whom you gave twelve gold coins and the silver dish that your mother, the blessed Silvia, had sent you with some gruel. And know that from that day when you gave to me with patience and a sincere heart, the Lord appointed you to be patriarch of his holy Church, for which he shed his own blood, and to be the successor and representative of Peter, the chief apostle.” The blessed Gregory said to him, “How do you know that the Lord then appointed me to be patriarch?” He answered, “Is it not because I am an angel of the Lord Almighty? That is why I know. For at that time the Lord had sent me to you to test your devotion: whether you showed mercy out of love for humanity, and not to be seen by people.” When the blessed man heard this, he was afraid, for he had never seen an angel before. He had been speaking to him as to a man and looking

at him. The angel said to the blessed man, “Do not be afraid. Behold, the Lord has sent me to be with you throughout this life.” When the blessed man heard this from the angel, he fell face down on the ground and worshiped the Lord, saying: “If, for that small gift, insignificant as it is, the most merciful Lord has shown me such abundant compassion as to send his angel to me to be with me always, what glory, then, will those who remain in his commandments be found worthy of, and those who do what is right! For he who said, ‘Mercy triumphs over judgment,’ does not lie. And whoever has mercy on the poor lends to God. The Lord of angels himself, who provides for human salvation, says to those standing at his right hand: ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world. For I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in. I was sick, and you visited me. I was naked, and you clothed me. I was in prison, and you came to me. Since you did this to one of these least of my brothers, you did it to me.’” May all of us who read and listen be granted to hear that blessed voice. And may we be made fellow sharers in the eternal blessings that God has prepared for those who love him
by Christ our God, for the sake of his most pure Mother, the holy Mother of God. For to him belong glory, honor, and worship, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
